2 Peter — Book introduction (Modern English candidate)

This letter is closely related to Peter's first letter.

Having described the blessings to which God calls Christians, the apostle urges those who have received these gifts to grow in grace and virtue.

He warns against false teachers, deceivers and people who mock the promised return of Christ.

He refutes their claims and explains why the great day of Christ's coming has been delayed.

The letter describes the solemn circumstances and consequences of that day, and calls believers to diligence, steadfast faith and holy living.

Original chapter outlineOriginal outlineVersesExhortations to add the exercise of various other graces to faith.1–11The apostle looks forward to his approaching decease.12–15And confirms the truth of the gospel, relating to Christ's appearing to judgment.16–21
Grow in the graces of living faith (verses 1–11)

Faith unites both weak and strong believers to Jesus Christ and truly purifies their hearts. Every sincere believer is justified before God through faith.

Faith produces genuine godliness, doing things no other grace can do in the soul.

Every fullness is found in Christ. Through the Holy Spirit he gives forgiveness, peace, grace, spiritual knowledge and new principles of life.

God's promises invite believers to ask whether they really have been made new inwardly and share in the divine nature.

Turn these promises into prayers for the Spirit's transforming and cleansing work.

Add knowledge to virtue by growing in understanding of God's complete truth and will.

Add self-control to knowledge: moderation in relation to this world's goods and pleasures.

Add patience to self-control: a cheerful submission to God's will amid troubles.

Suffering can produce patience, enabling us to carry crosses and losses with quiet submission.

Add godliness to patience: holy desires and affections that mark true worshipers.

Love your Christian brothers and sisters tenderly. They have the same Father and Master, belong to the same household, travel toward the same country and inherit the same kingdom.

Work to gain assurance of your calling and election through believing and doing what is right.

Such perseverance is evidence that God's mercy and grace sustain us so that we will not finally fall away.

Those diligent in living faith will enter the everlasting kingdom triumphantly, reigning with Christ forever.

It is in carrying out good works, not in pretending that works purchase acceptance, that believers should expect to approach this promised entrance.

Peter prepares for his death (verses 12–15)

We must become firmly established in the truth so that every changing opinion will not overturn us.

Pay special attention to those aspects of Christian truth most needed in our own day and to errors currently opposed to it.

The body is the soul's tent, a temporary dwelling that can be moved and taken down.

As death approaches, Peter grows more diligent in his appointed work.

Nothing makes death more peaceful than knowing we have sincerely followed Jesus and sought his glory.

Those who fear the Lord naturally speak of his loving kindness.

The enduring written word enables God's people to pass on the knowledge of him after they are gone.

Scripture is the Spirit-inspired word of God (verses 16–21)

The gospel is not weak speculation. It comes with divine power (Romans 1:16).

The law shows humanity's miserable condition under sin, but it does not provide the saving cure.

Jesus crucified, revealed in the gospel, heals the soul.

Rational arguments alone often fail to change a person ruled by greed, anger or lust. One piece of gold outweighs every argument for the greedy person; someone furious will not listen; a single tempting smile can defeat mere reasoning.

But the gospel announces Christ's precious blood, shed to save sinners from hell and to make satisfaction for their sins.

That message has the power to make believing hearts burn and to move even opponents, like Agrippa, toward recognizing its truth (Acts 26:28).

God is pleased with Christ and accepts people in him.

Old Testament prophets foretold both the promised Messiah and the gospel's salvation, speaking and writing through God's Spirit.

Their words provide a firm foundation for faith.

When the Spirit brings Scripture's light into a dark understanding, it is like daybreak spreading toward full daylight.

Everyone should study Scripture to understand its real meaning.

True Christians recognize God's word through the sweetness, spiritual power and divine glory they experience in it.

Fulfilled prophecies concerning Christ and his church testify to Christianity's truth.

The Holy Spirit inspired the prophets' actual words, guiding their communication so that what they wrote faithfully expressed what God had revealed.

The Scriptures must therefore be received and honored as the words of the Holy Spirit, with all their clarity, simplicity and power from God.

Receive the word in faith and cherish the Bible as a book written by holy people instructed by the Holy Spirit.
classic_reading:
[2Pet.1.1-2Pet.1.11]
2 Peter
This epistle clearly is connected with the former epistle of Peter. The apostle having stated the blessings to which God has called Christians, exhorts those who had received these precious gifts, to endeavour to improve in graces and virtues. They are urged to this from the wickedness of false teachers. They are guarded against impostors and scoffers, by disproving their false assertions, ch. 3:1-7, and by showing why the great day of Christ's coming was delayed, with a description of its awful circumstances and consequences; and suitable exhortations to diligence and holiness are given.
Chapter 1
Chapter Outline
Exhortations to add the exercise of various other graces to faith.
(1-11)
The apostle looks forward to his approaching decease.
(12-15)
And confirms the truth of the gospel, relating to Christ's appearing to judgment.
(16-21)
Verses 1-11
Faith unites the weak believer to Christ, as really as it does the strong one, and purifies the heart of one as truly as of another; and every sincere believer is by his faith justified in the sight of God. Faith worketh godliness, and produces effects which no other grace in the soul can do. In Christ all fulness dwells, and pardon, peace, grace, and knowledge, and new principles, are thus given through the Holy Spirit. The promises to those who are partakers of a Divine nature, will cause us to inquire whether we are really renewed in the spirit of our minds; let us turn all these promises into prayers for the transforming and purifying grace of the Holy Spirit. The believer must add knowledge to his virtue, increasing acquaintance with the whole truth and will of God. We must add temperance to knowledge; moderation about worldly things; and add to temperance, patience, or cheerful submission to the will of God. Tribulation worketh patience, whereby we bear all calamities and crosses with silence and submission. To patience we must add godliness: this includes the holy affections and dispositions found in the true worshipper of God; with tender affection to all fellow Christians, who are children of the same Father, servants of the same Master, members of the same family, travellers to the same country, heirs of the same inheritance. Wherefore let Christians labour to attain assurance of their calling, and of their election, by believing and well-doing; and thus carefully to endeavour, is a firm argument of the grace and mercy of God, upholding them so that they shall not utterly fall. Those who are diligent in the work of religion, shall have a triumphant entrance into that everlasting kingdom where Christ reigns, and they shall reign with him for ever and ever; and it is in the practice of every good work that we are to expect entrance to heaven.
[2Pet.1.12-2Pet.1.15]
Verses 12-15
We must be established in the belief of the truth, that we may not be shaken by every wind of doctrine; and especially in the truth necessary for us to know in our day, what belongs to our peace, and what is opposed in our time. The body is but a tabernacle, or tent, of the soul. It is a mean and movable dwelling. The nearness of death makes the apostle diligent in the business of life. Nothing can so give composure in the prospect, or in the hour, of death, as to know that we have faithfully and simply followed the Lord Jesus, and sought his glory. Those who fear the Lord, talk of his loving-kindness. This is the way to spread the knowledge of the Lord; and by the written word, they are enabled to do this.
[2Pet.1.16-2Pet.1.21]
Verses 16-21
The gospel is no weak thing, but comes in power, [Rom.1.16] Ro 1:16. The law sets before us our wretched state by sin, but there it leaves us. It discovers our disease, but does not make known the cure. It is the sight of Jesus crucified, in the gospel, that heals the soul. Try to dissuade the covetous worlding from his greediness, one ounce of gold weighs down all reasons. Offer to stay a furious man from anger by arguments, he has not patience to hear them. Try to detain the licentious, one smile is stronger with him than all reason. But come with the gospel, and urge them with the precious blood of Jesus Christ, shed to save their souls from hell, and to satisfy for their sins, and this is that powerful pleading which makes good men confess that their hearts burn within them, and bad men, even an Agrippa, to say they are almost persuaded to be Christians, [Acts.26.28] Ac 26:28. God is well pleased with Christ, and with us in him. This is the Messiah who was promised, through whom all who believe in him shall be accepted and saved. The truth and reality of the gospel also are foretold by the prophets and penmen of the Old Testament, who spake and wrote under influence, and according to the direction of the Spirit of God. How firm and sure should our faith be, who have such a firm and sure word to rest upon! When the light of the Scripture is darted into the blind mind and dark understanding, by the Holy Spirit of God, it is like the day-break that advances, and diffuses itself through the whole soul, till it makes perfect day. As the Scripture is the revelation of the mind and will of God, every man ought to search it, to understand the sense and meaning. The Christian knows that book to be the word of God, in which he tastes a sweetness, and feels a power, and sees a glory, truly divine. And the prophecies already fulfilled in the person and salvation of Christ, and in the great concerns of the church and the world, form an unanswerable proof of the truth of Christianity. The Holy Ghost inspired holy men to speak and write. He so assisted and directed them in delivering what they had received from him, that they clearly expressed what they made known. So that the Scriptures are to be accounted the words of the Holy Ghost, and all the plainness and simplicity, all the power and all the propriety of the words and expressions, come from God. Mix faith with what you find in the Scriptures, and esteem and reverence the Bible as a book written by holy men, taught by the Holy Ghost.

False teachers face certain judgment (verses 1–9)

The path of error is harmful, yet many people readily enter it.

Let us give Christ's enemies no valid reason to speak against his holy name or the salvation offered through him, the Way, Truth and Life.

False teachers deceive by using invented and manipulative words.

They lead others astray and bring judgment upon themselves.

God's dealings in earlier history illustrate his justice.

Angels were cast down from their dignity and glory because they disobeyed God.

Even creatures dwelling in heaven will suffer judgment if they sin.

Sin belongs to darkness; darkness is its deserved outcome.

God judged the ancient world in Noah's days. The number or social position of wrongdoers cannot make sin acceptable.

When wrongdoing spreads throughout a society, judgment may spread widely too.

God can turn fruitful land to desolation and flourishing cities into ashes.

No political strategy can prevent his judgment on unrepentant sin.

The God who preserves his servants through fire and water (Isaiah 43:2) can use the same elements in judgment.

When judgment falls upon the wicked, the Lord can preserve the righteous.

Living among evil people brings either grief over their sins or guilt through participating in them.

Yet God's children can remain faithful even in deeply corrupt surroundings, because Christ's grace within them is stronger than Satan's temptations or wicked examples.

God often places surprising obstacles in people's path before they commit sin, as though warning them to reconsider.

His wisdom and power ensure that his merciful purposes will be fulfilled.

Some wicked people escape visible punishment now because they are reserved for the day of judgment, when they will be punished with the devil and his angels.

The arrogance and corruption of deceptive teachers (verses 10–16)

False teachers and their followers abandon themselves to sensual desires.

They refuse to submit their thoughts to Christ's obedience, violate God's holy commands and go progressively deeper into impurity.

They also despise lawful authority God requires them to respect.

Their hearts are fixed upon temporary earthly gain, which they both desire and promise.

Those who presume upon God's grace as permission to indulge sin have special reason to tremble.

Some treat the moral demands of Scripture as though the gospel freed them from obeying God.

Christians should keep their distance from such teaching and conduct.

False promises of freedom lead to slavery (verses 17–22)

God's true word is living water that refreshes people who receive it.

False teachers resemble empty springs or clouds without rain, because they possess no saving truth.

As clouds can block the sunlight, false teaching can darken people's understanding with words lacking substance.

Because these deceivers spread darkness in this world, Henry says it is just that the mist of darkness should be their portion in the next.

While promising freedom, these teachers are themselves slaves of their sinful desires.

Their passions have conquered them completely.

Anyone entangled by sin is more easily overcome. Christians must remain close to God's word and beware people who confuse and mislead them.

Deliberate apostasy after knowledge is more serious than ignorance.

Speaking falsely against God's good way of salvation exposes a person to severe judgment.

This condition is dreadful. Yet Henry adds a critical qualification: it is not utterly without hope.

Just as a leper may be cleansed and a dead person raised, a person grieved by their departure from faith may still find mercy.

If your backsliding grieves you, believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved.
classic_reading:
[2Pet.2.1-2Pet.2.9]
Chapter 2
Chapter Outline
Believers are cautioned against false teachers, and the certainty of their punishment shown from examples. | (1-9) |
An account of these seducers, as exceedingly wicked. | (10-16) |
But as making high pretences to liberty and purity. | (17-22) |
Verses 1-9
Though the way of error is a hurtful way, many are always ready to walk therein. Let us take care we give no occasion to the enemy to blaspheme the holy name whereby we are called, or to speak evil of the way of salvation by Jesus Christ, who is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. These seducers used feigned words, they deceived the hearts of their followers. Such are condemned already, and the wrath of God abides upon them. God's usual method of proceeding is shown by examples. Angels were cast down from all their glory and dignity, for their disobedience. If creatures sin, even in heaven, they must suffer in hell. Sin is the work of darkness, and darkness is the wages of sin. See how God dealt with the old world. The number of offenders no more procures favour, than their quality. If the sin be universal, the punishment shall likewise extend to all. If in a fruitful soil the people abound in sin, God can at once turn a fruitful land into barrenness, and a well-watered country into ashes. No plans or politics can keep off judgments from a sinful people. He who keeps fire and water from hurting his people, [Isa.43.2] Is 43:2, can make either destroy his enemies; they are never safe. When God sends destruction on the ungodly, he commands deliverance for the righteous. In bad company we cannot but get either guilt or grief. Let the sins of others be troubles to us. Yet it is possible for the children of the Lord, living among the most profane, to retain their integrity; there being more power in the grace of Christ, and his dwelling in them, than in the temptations of Satan, or the example of the wicked, with all their terrors or allurements. In our intentions and inclinations to commit sin, we meet with strange hinderances, if we mark them When we intend mischief, God sends many stops to hinder us, as if to say, Take heed what you do. His wisdom and power will surely effect the purposes of his love, and the engagements of his truth; while wicked men often escape suffering here, because they are kept to the day of judgment, to be punished with the devil and his angels.
[2Pet.2.10-2Pet.2.16]
Verses 10-16
Impure seducers and their abandoned followers, give themselves up to their own fleshly minds. Refusing to bring every thought to the obedience of Christ, they act against God's righteous precepts. They walk after the flesh, they go on in sinful courses, and increase to greater degrees of impurity and wickedness. They also despise those whom God has set in authority over them, and requires them to honour. Outward temporal good things are the wages sinners expect and promise themselves. And none have more cause to tremble, than those who are bold to gratify their sinful lusts, by presuming on the Divine grace and mercy. Many such there have been, and are, who speak lightly of the restraints of God's law, and deem themselves freed from obligations to obey it. Let Christians stand at a distance from such.
[2Pet.2.17-2Pet.2.22]
Verses 17-22
The word of truth is the water of life, which refreshes the souls that receive it; but deceivers spread and promote error, and are set forth as empty, because there is no truth in them. As clouds hinder the light of the sun, so do these darken counsel by words wherein there is no truth. Seeing that these men increase darkness in this world, it is very just that the mist of darkness should be their portion in the next. In the midst of their talk of liberty, these men are the vilest slaves; their own lusts gain a complete victory over them, and they are actually in bondage. When men are entangled, they are easily overcome; therefore Christians should keep close to the word of God, and watch against all who seek to bewilder them. A state of apostacy is worse than a state of ignorance. To bring an evil report upon the good way of God, and a false charge against the way of truth, must expose to the heaviest condemnation. How dreadful is the state here described! Yet though such a case is deplorable, it is not utterly hopeless; the leper may be made clean, and even the dead may be raised. Is thy backsliding a grief to thee? Believe in the Lord Jesus, and thou shalt be saved.

Original chapter outlineOriginal outlineVersesThe design here is to remind of Christ's final coming to judgement.1–4He will appear unexpectedly, when the present frame of nature will be dissolved by fire.5–10From thence is inferred the need for holiness, and stedfastness in the faith.11–18
Scoffers deny Christ's promised return (verses 1–4)

Christians should have their purified minds awakened to active and joyful holiness.

In the gospel age scoffers will arise who make light of sin, mock salvation through Jesus Christ and ridicule his promised return.

A central teaching of faith concerns what God has promised, not what human beings can verify through past experience.

Scoffers will keep attacking that promise until Christ returns.

They see no dramatic change and therefore refuse to fear God (Psalm 55:19).

They assume that because God has not previously done something, he cannot do it or never will.

God's patience and the coming judgment (verses 5–10)

If the scoffers remembered God's judgment in the flood, they would not ridicule the warning of another world-wide judgment.

The same word that governed the ancient world has announced that the present heavens and earth will pass through fire.

This event is certain because God is truthful and powerful.

Human beings see an immense difference between a day and a thousand years. But all past, present and future are continually before God.

A delay of a thousand years is no more to him than our postponing something for an hour.

We struggle to understand eternity and wrongly imagine God must experience time as we do.

What people call slow fulfillment is actually divine patience.

It gives God's people time to grow in knowledge, holiness, faith, patience and good works, glorifying him by what they do and endure.

Everyone will give account of actions done in the body, whether good or evil.

Therefore live humbly, examine yourselves often and take final judgment seriously—even while others behave as though accountability would never come.

Christ will come unexpectedly, when people feel secure.

Splendid palaces and everything in which worldly people seek happiness will pass through judgment.

God's fire will consume what human sin has corrupted and refine what belongs to his work.

How foolish to make earthly possessions our ultimate portion when everything visible is passing away!

Seek happiness beyond this world.

Pursue holiness while growing in the knowledge of Christ (verses 11–18)

The certainty of Christ's return calls us to complete and universal holiness, not a minimal standard.

Genuine knowledge of Christ changes a person's life.

Believers await new heavens and a new earth, freed from present corruption and sin.

Only those clothed in Christ's righteousness and sanctified through the Holy Spirit will dwell there.

God is faithful to his promises.

Those whose sins are pardoned and who are reconciled to him are secure. Seek peace with all people, together with holiness.

Do not expect to face the Lord in peace if you spend the present day idle and careless.

We have work to complete before he calls us home.

The delay in his appearing should move us to faithful service, not impatience or moral carelessness.

Proud and corrupt people distort difficult passages of Scripture to suit their own views.

But the misuse of Paul's letters is no reason to discard them or any other part of the Bible. Human sin can twist every good divine gift.

When Scripture contains difficult teachings, prepare yourselves to understand them by obeying what is already clear.

Self-denial, distrust of our own pride and submission to Christ's authority are necessary if we are to embrace all gospel truth.

Reject human opinions that conflict with God's revealed law.

Those swept away by error lose their own steadfastness.

To remain firm, keep growing in faith, virtue, knowledge and every grace.

Seek not only to know more about Jesus Christ, but to become more like him and love him more deeply.

Such knowledge leads to thanksgiving and to praise that begins now and will continue forever.
classic_reading:
[2Pet.3.1-2Pet.3.4]
Chapter 3
Chapter Outline
The design here is to remind of Christ's final coming to judgement. | (1-4) |
He will appear unexpectedly, when the present frame of nature will be dissolved by fire. | (5-10) |
From thence is inferred the need for holiness, and stedfastness in the faith. | (11-18) |
Verses 1-4
The purified minds of Christians are to be stirred up, that they may be active and lively in the work of holiness. There will be scoffers in the last days, under the gospel, men who make light of sin, and mock at salvation by Jesus Christ. One very principal article of our faith refers to what only has a promise to rest upon, and scoffers will attack it till our Lord is come. They will not believe that he will come. Because they see no changes, therefore they fear not God, [Ps.55.19] Psa 55:19. What he never has done, they fancy he never can do, or never will do.
[2Pet.3.5-2Pet.3.10]
Verses 5-10
Had these scoffers considered the dreadful vengeance with which God swept away a whole world of ungodly men at once, surely they would not have scoffed at his threatening an equally terrible judgment. The heavens and the earth which now are, by the same word, it is declared, will be destroyed by fire. This is as sure to come, as the truth and the power of God can make it. Christians are here taught and established in the truth of the coming of the Lord. Though, in the account of men, there is a vast difference between one day and a thousand years, yet, in the account of God, there is no difference. All things past, present, and future, are ever before him: the delay of a thousand years cannot be so much to him, as putting off any thing for a day or for an hour is to us. If men have no knowledge or belief of the eternal God, they will be very apt to think him such as themselves. How hard is it to form any thoughts of eternity! What men count slackness, is long-suffering, and that to us-ward; it is giving more time to his own people, to advance in knowledge and holiness, and in the exercise of faith and patience, to abound in good works, doing and suffering what they are called to, that they may bring glory to God. Settle therefore in your hearts that you shall certainly be called to give an account of all things done in the body, whether good or evil. And let a humble and diligent walking before God, and a frequent judging of yourselves, show a firm belief of the future judgment, though many live as if they were never to give any account at all. This day will come, when men are secure, and have no expectation of the day of the Lord. The stately palaces, and all the desirable things wherein wordly-minded men seek and place their happiness, shall be burned up; all sorts of creatures God has made, and all the works of men, must pass through the fire, which shall be a consuming fire to all that sin has brought into the world, though a refining fire to the works of God's hand. What will become of us, if we set our affections on this earth, and make it our portion, seeing all these things shall be burned up? Therefore make sure of happiness beyond this visible world.
[2Pet.3.11-2Pet.3.18]
Verses 11-18
From the doctrine of Christ's second coming, we are exhorted to purity and godliness. This is the effect of real knowledge. Very exact and universal holiness is enjoined, not resting in any low measure or degree. True Christians look for new heavens and a new earth; freed from the vanity to which things present are subject, and the sin they are polluted with. Those only who are clothed with the righteousness of Christ, and sanctified by the Holy Ghost, shall be admitted to dwell in this holy place. He is faithful, who has promised. Those, whose sins are pardoned, and their peace made with God, are the only safe and happy people; therefore follow after peace, and that with all men; follow after holiness as well as peace. Never expect to be found at that day of God in peace, if you are lazy and idle in this your day, in which we must finish the work given us to do. Only the diligent Christian will be the happy Christian in the day of the Lord. Our Lord will suddenly come to us, or shortly call us to him; and shall he find us idle? Learn to make a right use of the patience of our Lord, who as yet delays his coming. Proud, carnal, and corrupt men, seek to wrest some things into a seeming agreement with their wicked doctrines. But this is no reason why St. Paul's epistles, or any other part of the Scriptures, should be laid aside; for men, left to themselves, pervert every gift of God. Then let us seek to have our minds prepared for receiving things hard to be understood, by putting in practice things which are more easy to be understood. But there must be self-denial and suspicion of ourselves, and submission to the authority of Christ Jesus, before we can heartily receive all the truths of the gospel, therefore we are in great danger of rejecting the truth. And whatever opinions and thoughts of men are not according to the law of God, and warranted by it, the believer disclaims and abhors. Those who are led away by error, fall from their own stedfastness. And that we may avoid being led away, we must seek to grow in all grace, in faith, and virtue, and knowledge. Labour to know Christ more clearly, and more fully; to know him so as to be more like him, and to love him better. This is the knowledge of Christ, which the apostle Paul reached after, and desired to attain; and those who taste this effect of the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, will, upon receiving such grace from him, give thanks and praise him, and join in ascribing glory to him now, in the full assurance of doing the same hereafter, for ever.
